description: We’re a team passionate about space exploration, technology, and building practical solutions. Our project focuses on using Mars surface data to help plan safer and more effective Marswalks. We’re looking for enthusiastic team members skilled in web development, UI/UX design, 3D visualization, data science, or machine learning who enjoy collaborating, solving problems, and turning ideas into working solutions.
summary:
MarsNav is an integrated Mars exploration platform developed to address one of the biggest challenges of future Mars missions: understanding the Martian environment and navigating its unpredictable terrain safely. Instead of relying on separate tools for different mission activities, MarsNav brings together NASA mission data, rover imagery, scientific analysis, and exploration technologies in one unified workspace. It incorporates imagery and mission information from Perseverance, Curiosity, Opportunity, and Spirit, allowing users to explore Martian regions, upload surface images, examine geological features, identify potential terrain hazards, and plan routes around obstacles. The platform includes dedicated modules for mission management, NASA data and live imagery, terrain intelligence, geological mapping, 3D terrain exploration, base camp selection, astronaut mobility, environmental monitoring, radiation assessment, and EVA route planning.
MarsNav aims to transform complex planetary data into practical exploration insights. It can help researchers understand potential landing and exploration sites, support safer rover navigation, and assist mission planners in evaluating environmental risks. Looking ahead, we envision MarsNav becoming a unified decision-support workspace for future human missions, helping astronauts make better-informed decisions before and during exploration of the Red Planet.
details: MarsNav is an AI-powered Martian terrain exploration and navigation platform designed to support safer rover and astronaut missions. It integrates NASA imagery and scientific datasets to analyze surface terrain, identify rocks, boulders and potential hazards, assess environmental risks, and plan optimized routes across Martian landscapes. The platform includes mission configuration, NASA raw imagery, terrain intelligence, hazard analysis, risk assessment, surface mission dashboards, multilayer geological mapping, safety and environmental monitoring, geological targets, suit mobility analysis, and astronaut route planning. It uses computer vision, image processing, terrain analysis, and A* pathfinding to support exploration decisions. The project was developed using React, JavaScript, CSS, Vite, NASA APIs and datasets, Gemini API, and cloud deployment through Vercel. Its creative approach combines multiple scientific data sources and interactive analysis tools into one workspace. The intended impact is to help researchers and future mission planners understand Martian terrain, identify potential dangers, and make better-informed exploration and navigation decisions. Key considerations include data accuracy, NASA data provenance, route safety, usability, and avoiding fabricated scientific measurements.
